title: OpenMontage ARCHITECTURE.md
claims: The architecture document describes OpenMontage as an agent-orchestrated platform in which an LLM coding assistant reads pipeline manifests and skills, calls Python tools, writes JSON checkpoints, self-reviews, and can request human approval; it says there is no runtime Python orchestrator.

The repository layout includes Python infrastructure, video tools, YAML pipeline definitions, JSON schemas for artifacts/checkpoints/pipelines/styles/tools, Markdown skills, Remotion composer, and tests.

The checked config.yaml exposes LLM provider fields for anthropic, openai, gemini, openrouter, ollama, mistral, and minimax; the architecture document separately says the coding assistant is the control plane, so the field list does not by itself prove a runtime LLM API call.
Tool contracts include dependencies, input/output schemas, fallback_tools, agent_skills, resource_profile, retry_policy, seed, and model.

The stated required system dependencies are Python >=3.10 and FFmpeg; optional dependencies include Node.js for Remotion, GPU/CUDA for local generation, Piper, ManimCE, and Mermaid CLI. Python core packages include pyyaml, pydantic, jsonschema, and python-dotenv.

Checkpoints persist stage, status, artifacts, review, and cost_snapshot; the document states that schema validation occurs before checkpoint writing and that a failed stage can resume from the last checkpoint.

resources.gpu: Only local video/image generation requires GPU/CUDA; orchestration and FFmpeg path are not assigned a GPU requirement
resources.workflow: research -> proposal -> script -> scene_plan -> assets -> edit -> compose

limitations: The architecture document is a design and source exploration document; it does not provide L4/A100 end-to-end timing, peak RAM/VRAM, or independent quality scores.
providers: provider selectors and fallback tools are declared in tool contracts

title: OpenMontage README
claims: The README lists complete pipelines including Animated Explainer, Animation, Avatar Spokesperson, Cinematic, Clip Factory, Documentary Montage, Hybrid, Localization & Dub, Podcast Repurpose, Screen Demo, and Talking Head.

Each pipeline follows research -> proposal -> script -> scene_plan -> assets -> edit -> compose; the agent reads stage-director skills, self-reviews, checkpoints, and asks for human approval at creative decision points.
The README says reference videos can be analyzed for transcript, pacing, scenes, keyframes, and style, then returned with concepts, tool route, cost estimates, and a sample before full production.

The documented governance includes human gates, pre-compose validation for delivery promise/slideshow risk/renderer family, post-render ffprobe/frame/audio/subtitle checks, provider decision trails, and budget estimate/reserve/reconcile controls.

README demo claims include The Last Banana as a 60-second short using six Kling v3 clips via fal.ai, Google Chirp3-HD narration, captions, Remotion, and total cost $1.33; Void as four GPT Image images, TTS, music, WhisperX subtitles, and total cost $0.69.

resources.gpu: Only provider-specific local generation paths require GPU; Remotion/FFmpeg composition can be local CPU paths
resources.workflow: agent reads manifest and skills -> tools -> self-review -> checkpoint -> human gate -> render

limitations: Demo durations and costs are author claims; this report did not rerun them or independently inspect video quality.

title: OpenMontage PROVIDERS.md
claims: The ComfyUI video tool accepts a local ComfyUI server URL and bundled or caller-supplied workflows; the document explicitly lists a MiniMax H3 official open-weight local workflow with pruned INT8 diffusion model, Qwen3-VL text encoder, video VAE, and audio VAE.

ComfyUI Partner Node entries are separate hosted execution paths: Gemini Omni Flash about $0.146/sec, Seedance 2.5 about $0.148/sec at 480p or $0.333/sec at 720p, and MiniMax H3 API about $0.129/sec at 768P or $0.186/sec at 2K; the local MiniMax H3 graph is listed as no API charge.
Partner Nodes require current ComfyUI, network access, a logged-in Comfy account, and prepaid credits; actual metered usage is authoritative.

The local video section lists CUDA tools wan_video, hunyuan_video, cogvideo_video, and ltx_video_local. The model table lists Wan2.2 TI2V-5B 12GB, Wan2.1 1.3B 6GB, Wan2.1 14B 24GB, Hunyuan 1.5 12GB, LTX-2 8GB, CogVideo 5B 10GB, and CogVideo 2B 6GB classes.

The document describes Wan clips as roughly five-second passes, with longer duration implemented by chaining segments and dropping the duplicated seam frame; it warns that chaining can drift in contrast and colour.

For a 12GB path, the document records a measured 1.97GB peak for sequential offload at 704x480, with approximately 4 seconds per denoising step of PCIe traffic; this is a provider-document example, not an L4/A100 benchmark.

resources.resolution: 704x480 example; local table also labels 720p @ 24fps for Wan2.2 TI2V-5B
resources.time_s: ~4 seconds per denoising step of PCIe traffic in the 12GB sequential-offload example
resources.precision: Local H3 pruned INT8 stack; local video precision auto/bf16/int8/int4 options
resources.workflow: comfyui_video local workflow or hosted Partner Node; wan_video text/image/video/first_last_frame operations

title: H3 Lite README
claims: H3 Lite is a Codex/WorkBuddy skill for local MiniMax H3 generation through ComfyUI; the agent chooses a route, prepares components, generates native-audio video, and checks results.
The main supported route is Windows + NVIDIA + ComfyUI; macOS is a community route, Linux + NVIDIA is experimental, and no claim is made for a general remote endpoint.

The skill routes T2VA, I2VA, FL2VA, and Ref2VA tasks and saves anchor cards in anchors.json while manifest.json records the path; anchor_qa checks first/middle/last frames and human review is still required for identity/clothing/composition.
Set A uses W4A8 diffusion plus a 4B INT4 text encoder; Set B uses a 4B FP8 text encoder. The default fast profile is 4 steps, 640x352, native audio; balanced is 6 steps and quality is 8 steps.
With the same Set B, compatible workflow, prompt, seed, 640x352, and 4 steps, the README reports RTX 4060 Ti 16GB + 32GB RAM at about 77.08s and RTX 4070 Laptop 8GB + 32GB RAM at about 591.22s.

The README lists a first validation as a 5-second simple red-ball video and says multi-shot tasks should first run at low resolution; it includes sample MP4 artifacts and an assets-rolling-redball release.

resources.resolution: 640x352 default; README also lists 864x480 and larger profiles

resources.precision: Set A W4A8/INT4; Set B FP8 text encoder
